title: Arthur Whetsel, Freddy Jenkins and the trumpet section
summary: Artie had a beautiful tone but little power; Duke switched parts around; Freddy Jenkins was a peculiar stylist and good section man.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, listen, along the lines of talking about different musicians that you worked with and so on, so let's talk about some of them while their names come up and while you were working with them. What would you say about Artie? I know you're going to say he had a beautiful tone.
Yeah. Well, he had a beautiful tone. That's one thing I could say about him. He had a real beautiful tone.
He didn't have a strong tone.
No.
He didn't have a lot of power, did he?
No. But a beautiful tone.
Well, was Artie playing the first parts all the time?
Yeah. He played a lot of the first parts. Well, I'll tell you, Duke switched parts around.
That's what I thought.
Yeah. On one number, sometimes I'd be playing second, I'd be playing first, and like that, on the same tune.
Yeah.
He'd switch the parts around.
Switch the parts around. What happened
No. That's the way he would write it.
Oh, he would write it that way.
Yeah.

I see. Well, for instance -- because on any of those numbers where the band was really -- where the brass section was really blowing out, all out, and the band was driving, I mean, Artie couldn't have played those.
No. He would give it to me.
Yeah. He'd give it to you. Well, now Posey never played a first part, ever, did he?
Very seldom.
No. Freddie Jenkins. Well, really, Freddie -- he just brought Freddie in for a little color here or there, didn't he?
But he could play.
Could he?
Yeah.
Could he really?
Yeah. He had a peculiar style, but he could play.
Well, what kind of a style did he have?
I don't know. I don't know how to explain it, but he had a peculiar style. He could play.
You mean it wasn't a straightforward thing. It was more of like an acquired -- like an olive, or something?
I think you should have records with him playing on it.
Yeah, I have. I'm just trying to get the words out of you. I know -- I do know how he sounded. Well, of course, one thing was he wasn't real powerful, Cootie.
No.
But he could improvise, though, couldn't he?
Yeah.
Yeah. He could improvise, which after all is the crux of the thing.
Yeah.
Yeah.
And he was a very good section man.
Was he?
Yeah. A very good section man.
Why? In what way?
About getting things together and blending in with the section.
